messages:
cheng-wu: Quick heads-up — us-east-gpu-3 reported an ECC error burst and sustained XID spikes starting ~22:17 UTC. Proposing a 'soft-quarantine' flow: cordon immediately, allow running Kubernetes pods / Slurm jobs to finish for 15m-30m, then drain+replace if errors persist. Thoughts? :thinking:

infra-bot: Alert: ECC_RATE(us-east-gpu-3) = 0.72 (threshold 0.5). XID spikes = 48/min. Node health score fell to 0.32. Tags: gpu-rt, prod-tier.

rachel: +1 to cordon-first. We should avoid noisy evictions on long training jobs. Maybe default to 30m for Slurm batch nodes, 15m for k8s inference.

samuel: For k8s inference, we should have an opt-out label so latency-sensitive services can fall back to spare-pool immediately. Suggest label: `no-soft-quarantine=true`.

jay: Can we distinguish transient ECC blips vs progressive degradation? Need hysteresis rules. If ECC drops <0.3 for 10m -> auto uncordon. If it stays >0.5 -> escalate.

sophia: Proposed rule set (initial):
- ECC_rate > 0.5 for 5m -> cordon node immediately.
- If ECC_rate > 0.5 persists for 30m -> drain + replace node.
- If XID > 100 in 10m -> immediate drain (safety-critical).
- First rollout should be a canary (10 nodes) and a kill-switch operator flag.

alex: FYI cost note — replacing nodes frequently adds ~$120/node (procurement & telemetry + lost work). If we can reuse warm spare nodes or schedule replacements in batches we save a lot. Also consider delaying replacements for low-utilization windows.

ops-oncall: Need a runbook link and a manual rollback/kill-switch. Please add a "panic-drain" toggle in Console for oncall to force immediate eviction + replacement and automate customer notifications for Dedicated pools.

sophia: Manual ops snippets for quick intervention:

```
# kubernetes
kubectl cordon gpu-node-xyz
kubectl drain gpu-node-xyz --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --timeout=15m
\n# slurm
scontrol update NodeName=gpu-node-123 State=POWER_DOWN Reason="ECC burst auto-quarantine"
sinfo -R
```

samuel: Also ask monitoring to enrich metrics: ECC per-GPU, XID per-GPU, memtest errors, last thermal trip timestamp, and average retry count. Keep 7d retention for triage.

rachel: I'll draft the orchestration PR with these thresholds and the opt-out label. Plan a small canary tomorrow 07:00 UTC in us-east: 10% nodes, oncall + pagerduty notified.

cheng-wu: Thanks — I'll open the RFC and include the cost/sla tradeoffs and the replacement batching plan. Tagging @ops-oncall for runbook details. We'll test in staging tonight (simulate ECC spikes).

infra-bot: Note: feature-flag 'soft-quarantine' currently OFF. Scheduled canary enable at 2027-03-08T07:00:00Z for us-east experiment.

ops-oncall: ack. Please add step-by-step in runbook: customer notification template, console panic-drain flow, how to rollback flag, and how to remap traffic to spare pools.
